# Independent review: exact radial carrier and closed energy operators

Date: 2026-09-17.
Reviewer: /root/pairzero_geometry_review.
Verdict: ACCEPT_EXACT_RADIAL_CLOSED_OPERATOR_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.
Disposition: no mathematical correction required in C1--C7.

## 1. Frozen candidate and scope

Reviewed complete candidate:
`RADIAL_CLOSED_OPERATOR_PREFLIGHT.md`
SHA256: `e3881205c3c14814cee060b86e1773dc1701e6ea839213fef4bbb22bd5e65faf`
Bytes: 8809. LF: 189.
Candidate source base: `07cf0e5892ec9b0bf53a70701dffc0d85100df53`.

This review accepts an obstruction to one precise realization: a single
closed, or closable, complex-linear energy transform on the exact radial
carrier H=L2([0,infinity),ds), with g_z(s)=f(sqrt(s+z^2)). It also accepts
the corresponding obstruction to closed or closable nonnegative forms
on this same H. It does not establish either sign of the original V.

The review is analytic and source-bound. No numerical test, Lean proof,
new literature premise, search, descendant agent, repository mutation,
Pro dispatch, or RH claim forms part of it.

## 2. Direct input bindings

The named inputs were read directly in the isolated worktree and their
hashes rechecked against the candidate:

- `REPORT_2026-09-17_RADIAL_GRAM_DIVISOR_PREFLIGHT.md`, Q2--Q3:
  `8fffcd6f46c4228fec6703864920e3e6121cee3c51a2d2025ec6b7b0a78652ad`.
- `REPORT_2026-09-14_FULL_V_RANK_TWO_INTAKE.md`, R3--R7:
  `51168fb802d7facfb74291d0a3fc0009b121f540711df2fe10ae01cd84c1d14f`.
- `REPORT_2026-09-16_LOGVCURV_INTAKE.md`, I1:
  `074a6ee11edf58ed502f8a41454515c06b5d286605b53ff0fe9e889981a3b929`.

The previously independently reviewed quotient-continuation lemma is
used only in its already accepted scope, specialized to denominator 1.
In particular, the current argument does not assume positivity of V as
an unconditional source fact.

## 3. C1--C2: exact carrier, strict interaction, conditional feature

PASS. The even holomorphic source makes f(sqrt(s+z^2)) branch independent.
The earlier full-strip Hilbert-valued bounds provide the H-holomorphic
map g on S={|Im z|<pi/4}; the present proof uses that result without
altering the carrier, tail, or measure. The identity g_z=g_(-z) is exact.

The source statements used about V are distinct from all-family PSD:
V is jointly holomorphic on S times S, has the stated real symmetry,
and satisfies, for every nonzero real a,

    V(-a,-a)=V(a,a)>0,
    0<V(a,-a)<V(a,a).

Indeed, the prior strict two-node comparison gives V(a,-a)<G(a,-a),
while g_a=g_(-a) gives G(a,-a)=G(a,a)=V(a,a). Strict squared-coordinate
log concavity supplies the strict inequality; evenness alone does not.

Hypothesizing C2 gives PSD of every finite matrix V(x_i,x_j) with x_i
in I. The accepted Q3 lemma applies with N=V and D=1: its denominator
condition holds everywhere, and the strip is conjugation-stable and
simply connected. Thus the global holomorphic feature F satisfying
<F(z),F(w)>=V(conj(z),w) is a conditional consequence of C2. It is not a
proof that the actual source kernel is PSD on I or on the whole strip.

The conventions of holomorphy and inner products are consistent:
inner products are conjugate-linear in the first argument, so a fixed
first-slot vector defines a complex-linear scalar functional in the
second slot.

## 4. C3: same actual output Hilbert space

PASS. The identification with the proposed operator's actual codomain
is necessary and is proved, rather than presumed.

Let E0 be the closed linear span of F(I). If e is perpendicular to E0,
then <e,F(z)> is holomorphic and vanishes on I. A real interval has
accumulation points inside S, so the scalar identity theorem applies.
It follows that F(S) lies in E0.

For any finite coefficient row, C2 and C4 equate the squared norms of
sum c_i F(x_i) and sum c_i T g_(x_i). Consequently a zero combination
on the feature side gives a zero combination in K. The stated map U
is therefore well-defined and isometric. Its extension to E0 is bounded
and complex linear, with range equal to the closed span of the actual
operator outputs. The map F_tilde=UF is consequently holomorphic into
that fixed K, and F_tilde(x)=Tg_x for every x in the original interval.

No arbitrary gluing of different output spaces, surjectivity onto all
of K, or assumption of boundedness of T on H is used.

## 5. C4: analytic continuation through the closed graph

PASS. This is the decisive step, and it handles the original negative
interval correctly.

The graph of a closed linear operator is a closed complex subspace of
H direct-sum K, whether or not its domain is dense. Both components of
Psi(z)=(g_z,F_tilde(z)) are holomorphic. For any b perpendicular to the
graph, <b,Psi(z)> is holomorphic and is zero on I. The identity theorem
makes it zero on the connected strip. Taking the double orthogonal
complement yields Psi(S) contained in Graph(T).

Hence all the global domain assertions are conclusions:

    g_z belongs to Dom(T), and T g_z=F_tilde(z), for every z in S.

In particular, positive shifts were not added to the original domain
hypothesis. Although x and -x are not both in the original negative I,
closedness and analytic continuation force the operator relation across
zero. This validates the subsequent use of the pair a,-a.

Since g_a=g_(-a) and T is single-valued, F_tilde(a)=F_tilde(-a). The
preserved Gram identity therefore forces V(a,-a)=V(a,a), contradicting
the independently established strict inequality for a nonzero real a.
The contradiction is valid for any nonempty real open starting interval.
No unbounded-operator interchange of T with an integral or derivative
has been performed.

## 6. C5: closable operators and nonnegative forms

PASS. If T is closable, its graph closure is the graph of a single-valued
closed linear operator extending T. The original identities are retained
on every g_x in I, so the same contradiction applies.

For a nonnegative complex sesquilinear form q, positivity gives Hermitian
symmetry by polarization, and Cauchy--Schwarz makes its null space the
radical. Thus the quotient of the domain by null(q), completed in its
energy norm, is a legitimate Hilbert space K. The class map T is linear
and satisfies <Tu,Tv>=q(u,v).

The candidate's direct graph argument is sound. If u_n tends to u in H
and Tu_n tends to v in K, then

    ||u_n-u_m||_H^2 + q(u_n-u_m,u_n-u_m) -> 0.

Completeness in the form norm supplies a limit u_* in the form domain.
The H limit identifies u_*=u, and the energy limit identifies Tu=v.
Thus T is closed without any density requirement or square-root theorem.
This reduces C7 to the already excluded operator realization.

The closable-form assertion has the same scope. Equivalently, the usual
sequential closability criterion says that u_n->0 in H and an energy-
Cauchy sequence force q(u_n,u_n)->0. It makes the energy class map T
closable: a graph limit (0,v) must have v=0. Its closed operator extension
is then excluded. This also verifies the conclusion without appealing
to a densely defined self-adjoint representation of q.

## 7. C6--C7: Gaussian control and exact no-go boundary

PASS. For the control f_a(u)=exp(-a u^2), a>0,

    d/dt exp(-a((t+x)^2+(t+y)^2))
      = -2a(2t+x+y) exp(-a((t+x)^2+(t+y)^2)).

The full integral therefore equals exp(-a(x^2+y^2))/(2a). Directly,
G_a integrates exp(-2as-a(x^2+y^2)) over s>=0 and has exactly the same
value. The identity operator is a valid realization for that control.
Its squared-coordinate logarithm is linear, so the strict source
inequality needed for the contradiction is absent. The sanity check
correctly demonstrates that the proof is not a generic objection to
evenness or radial coordinates.

The resulting exclusion includes nonlocal or unbounded closed linear
operators on this precise H; it is not limited to multiplication or
bounded integral kernels. It does not exclude a carrier retaining shift
orientation, an enlarged input carrier with additional information,
shift-dependent or nonlinear realizations, or purely algebraic
nonclosable maps. The latter are outside the theorem, not certified
alternatives.

No finite negative row of the original V is exhibited. No positive lower
bound for V is proved. An abstract positive feature, if V were PSD, need
not be induced by a closed operator on this radial H; the obstruction
therefore does not refute PSD of V. Source properties and prior two-node
comparisons remain valid and useful within their stated scopes.

## Final disposition

ACCEPT_EXACT_RADIAL_CLOSED_OPERATOR_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY, bound to the exact
candidate bytes and hashes above. No correction required. The new
isometric identification and closed-graph continuation are valid; together
they rule out the specified exact radial-carrier energy realizations.
Full V positivity and RH remain open. This acceptance is an analytic
review, not Lean validation, canonical admission, or a new proof dispatch.
accepted: C1--C4: no single closed linear operator from the exact radial L2 carrier to any Hilbert space can reproduce original V on I; unbounded and nondense-domain operators are included
C5: closable operators and nonnegative closed or closable energy forms on that fixed carrier are likewise excluded
C6: the Gaussian control admits identity transform, so target asymmetry rather than source evenness alone supplies the contradiction

isometry well-defined on every finite complex row and extends to fixed actual codomain
closed Graph(T) membership propagates from negative I to all S by scalar identity
g_z=g_-z would force V(a,-a)=V(a,a), contradicting the independently accepted strict two-node inequality
closed energy form gives closed class-map operator by graph-norm completeness
